territorial_scope.description: Applies to licensees under the Malaysian class licence, including foreign individuals and foreign companies, which must appoint a Malaysia-based local representative.

evidence.quote: the Foreign Licensee shall appoint a local representative

summary.short: Declaration No. 87 of 2025 dispenses with the registration formality for internet messaging and social media service providers under the Applications Service Provider class licence, deeming them registered from 1 January 2026. Declaration No. 88 of 2025 sets standard licence conditions for class licensees.
summary.long: Declaration No. 87 of 2025, made under sections 13, 44, 46A and 126 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, dispenses with the formality of registration for the class of persons providing Internet Messaging Services and Social Media Services under the Applications Service Provider Class Licence. Persons operating under the class licence are deemed registered as at 1 January 2026, and persons still registered under it become deemed licensees upon expiry of their registration. The declaration does not apply to persons exempted under paragraphs 5(e) and (f) of the Exemption Order 2000. The companion Declaration No. 88 of 2025 makes standard licence conditions in its Annex A binding on persons registered as class licensees: compliance with written laws, subsidiary legislation and consumer codes; an indemnity to the Minister and the Commission; and, for foreign licensees, a local representative who serves as point of contact, accepts legal notices and assists with directions, including on removal or blocking of content, and who must be kept available at all times. Changes to the local representative must be notified immediately.

notes: The document contains two instruments: Declaration No. 87 of 2025 (deemed registration from 1 January 2026, the subject of this file) and its companion Declaration No. 88 of 2025 with Annex A standard conditions. Neither text refers to the other, so no relation between them is coded. Relations cover only text stated in the document. Text extraction is damaged: the dates and the Declaration No. 88 number are illegible (e.g. the Declaration No. 87 dateline and the Declaration No. 88 dateline and number), the Declaration No. 88 licence number is partly garbled, and Annex A numbering is out of order. Verify these against the official PDF. Declaration No. 87 uses the term Class Licence for the Regulations 2000 class, while Declaration No. 88 uses the Applications Services Provider Class Licence, Licence No. ASP/C/2025/1; the text does not state these are the same. Internet Messaging Services and Social Media Services are not defined in the document.
